FE.thesis_one_line: Ohio-area regulated electric utility rebuilding trust after a settled bribery scandal, priced for far less growth than its own guidance.
kill_criteria: FY2026 Core EPS guidance cut below the current $2.62 low end in any quarterly release.

Consolidated net debt/EBITDA rises above 5.5x (per the 10-Q debt schedule) without a disclosed, credible deleveraging plan tied to Energize365 financing. [DV17 2026-10-10: net debt incl. $1,376m short-term borrowings is $28.9bn, 5.3x on the d4 EBITDA of $5.42bn; EBITDA definition must be stated (filing-based OI + depreciation is about $4.0bn)]
An adverse verdict, or new DOJ/SEC action, arising from the January 2027 criminal trial of former executives.
A single unplanned equity issuance diluting shares outstanding by more than 5% versus the financing plan disclosed at the time of the $36bn capital-plan announcement.
Two additional consecutive quarters of GAAP operating losses (as derived for Q4 2025) without a primary-source explanation in the 10-K/10-Q reconciliation.
key_adverse_facts: TTM free cash flow is approximately -$2.01bn; the 5-year capital plan was just raised ~30% to $36bn, and financing is not yet fully disclosed.
Derived Q4 2025 GAAP operating loss (~-$24M) and net loss (~-$49M), despite a positive full-year Core (non-GAAP) EPS of $2.55.
Guidance was not raised at either Q1 or Q2 2026 despite ~10%+ revenue growth in both quarters.

A criminal trial of two former executives (Chuck Jones, Mike Dowling) is set for jury selection 21 January 2027, and the current 10-Q references an ongoing securities class action without a stated resolution.
[DV17 2026-10-10] Net debt is $28.9bn including $1,376m of short-term borrowings (not $27.5bn); 5.3x on the d4 EBITDA, which could not be reproduced from the filings.
data_conflicts: The Q4 2025 GAAP operating/net loss is derived (FY2025 10-K less nine months); [DV17 2026-10-10] the driver is the ~$275m ($213m after tax) Ohio restitution and refunds recognized in Q4 2025 (10-Q Note 9), not pension MTM.

GNRC.thesis_one_line: Backup-generator maker with a real, SEC-filed Amazon data-center supply deal, but the stock jumped about 18% in one session on the news and now prices in more than a fair base case. [Corrected 2026-10-08 DV19: earlier text said 40%.]
kill_criteria: Residential segment net sales decline resumes or deepens for two consecutive quarters.
The disclosed data-center/hyperscale order backlog (currently $1.6bn per the Q2 2026 release) fails to grow, or is reduced/cancelled, in a subsequent 10-Q or 8-K.
FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance is cut below the current 20.0%-21.0% range.
Net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises above 3.0x (from ~1.4x currently) without a clearly disclosed link to funding confirmed hyperscale capacity.
A future filing shows Amazon's cumulative gross payments materially missing the disclosed $2.4bn 2027-2028 initial-delivery plan (the warrant-vesting disclosure is the natural tripwire).
key_adverse_facts: The core Residential segment is still shrinking year-over-year (-2% in Q2 2026, +1% in Q1 2026) — the home-standby recovery the triage flagged for verification has not materialized.
Only $2.4bn of the headline '$8bn' Amazon framework is delivery-dated (2027-2028); the remainder is unproven optionality.
Approximately 150bps of the FY2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raise is an explicitly one-time Section 301 tariff refund, not organic operating leverage.
Share buybacks were paused (zero repurchases in Q1 and Q2 2026) despite a new $500M, 24-month authorization approved in February 2026.
data_conflicts: Adjusted EPS was only available from primary sources for the two most recent quarters plus Q4 2025; older quarters in the 8-quarter table are GAAP-only from SEC XBRL.
The Q2 2026 10-Q references Zawaski et al. v. General Power Systems, Inc. litigation without a visible exposure amount in the excerpt reviewed.
GNRC.confidence_in_thesis: low-medium - the Amazon catalyst is verified and economically real (warrant vesting is tied to actual payments), but only a fraction of the disclosed framework is delivery-dated and the reverse DCF shows limited margin of safety after the +18% single-day re-rating [Corrected 2026-10-08 DV19: earlier text said 40%]

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for GNRC (outside V1's 69-name universe). The analyst's reverse DCF implies a ~13.5%/yr 10-year adjusted-EPS CAGR to justify the price, above an honest base case of ~10.5%/yr built from the confirmed 2027-2028 delivery schedule plus a flattish Residential segment.

GNRC.scenario_basis: FY2026E adjusted EPS ~$8.10; bear 2%/base 10.5%/bull 22% EPS CAGR; exit P/E 14x/18x/22x; no dividend; 9.5% discount rate reflecting beta 1.91.

HPE.thesis_one_line: Server and networking OEM whose AI-server and Juniper-networking businesses keep beating raised guidance, at a valuation still below a fair base case.
kill_criteria: Non-GAAP EPS guidance cut from the current FY2026 $3.75-$3.85 range in any subsequent quarterly release.
Networking segment (Juniper) growth decelerates sharply (e.g., below 20% YoY) once the Juniper base is fully in both comparison periods.
Consolidated net debt/EBITDA (per the 10-Q's own debt schedule) rises above ~2.5x without a disclosed deleveraging path.
Disclosed evidence of AI-server order/backlog growth stalling, or loss of a major hyperscale customer.
Reopening of the Juniper merger review (e.g., a successful appeal of the August 2026 Tunney Act approval) that reimposes conditions beyond the already-completed Instant On divestiture.
key_adverse_facts: FY2025 GAAP net income was only $57M on $34.3bn of revenue, with a full-year GAAP operating loss of -$437M; the FY2025 fiscal-Q2 GAAP net loss of $1.05bn (-$0.82/share) is not fully explained from primary sources reviewed in this session.
Net debt/EBITDA is approximately 2.0x from the debt-funded $14bn Juniper acquisition.

Actual Q3 FY2026 non-GAAP EPS beat the top of the company's own prior-quarter guidance by roughly 19%, suggesting guidance-setting is struggling to keep pace with demand — strong momentum but weaker predictability.

The DOJ-required Instant On WLAN divestiture drew reported bids as low as $1-15 million, and the presiding judge questioned whether the remedy was a genuine structural fix before approving the settlement in August 2026.
data_conflicts: Organic (ex-Juniper) revenue growth cannot be cleanly separated from the primary sources reviewed; Networking's +74.9% YoY growth conflates organic demand with the Juniper acquisition entering the comparison base.
The FY2025 fiscal-Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.44 used in the dossier's table is implied algebraically from the FY2026 Q3 release's stated YoY change, not independently confirmed from the FY2025 10-Q.
